newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ANGRY LLOYD DISMAYED BY ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ANGRY LLOYD DISMAYED BY ENGLAND.

text.p: England coach David Lloyd plans to read the riot act to certain players following Zimbabwe's victory in the one-day series on Wednesday.
Lloyd accused his team of not being "up" for the game which saw England go 2-0 down in the best-of-three series and admitted they were under-performing badly abroad.
"I think they were up for it more than our players. That's a hard thing to say, but I've just said it.
"What disappoints me most is that we show no consistency.
"We continue to put little pockets of play together, where we play well, but not the whole.
"These players are in a position to put it right and they have a responsibility for the way they play on the pitch.
"As far as England are concerned we've got a lot of work to do. The game was there for the taking and we weren't up to it."

"It's been said often that England don't travel well and that's something we have to work on. We did really well to beat India and Pakistan in England, but we need to play better abroad, it's as simple as that".
Former test captain Bob Willis described England on television as "an embarrassment", but Zimbabwe captain Alistair Campbell was understandably jubilant at his side's triumph.
"It's hard to put this feeling into words. It hasn't really sunk in yet. But we knew we were capable of doing it and now we have shown the cricket world we are able to compete at top level.
"We have some very good individual players in our side. The gurus have been saying all tour that we are a good fielding side, but I don't think they give us enough credit".

"If you talk to the players from the sub-continent who have played us quite a bit they will tell you that Heath Streak and Paul Strang are really good bowlers and that Dave Houghton and Andy Flower are good batsmen".

"It's hard to put into words what it means to win a series for the first time. When we came back from Pakistan a few months ago the public were really on our back because we had lost and they thought we were rubbish".
"I had to stay indoors because if I went out to the pub or a restaurant I just got an ear bashing. But cricket fans are fickle and beating England has turned us into heroes, I suppose".
Match referee Hanumant Singh was less impressed by the home side, issuing a severe reprimand to Campbell, Andy Flower and Craig Evans for excessive appealing.
The trio were upset when an appeal for a catch behind against Nasser Hussain was rejected. Singh also reprimanded the England team for excessive appealing during the first test in Bulawayo.
